newsitem.title: CHINA: Chronology of life of China paramount leader Deng.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of life of China paramount leader Deng.

text.p: The following is a chronology of the life of Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, who died late on Wednesday at the age of 92.
August 22, 1904 - Deng Xiaoping is born as Deng Xixian, the son of a local landlord and his concubine in Guang'an county in China's southwestern Sichuan province.
1920 - Leaves China to join a work-study programme in France, where he acquired a taste for croissants and worked in factories near Paris and at the Renault plant in Billancourt.
1922 - Joins the Communist Youth League while in Paris.
1924 - Joins the Chinese Communist Party.
1926 - Studies briefly in Moscow before returning to China.

1927 - Becomes secretary to the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party despite his youth and changes his name to Deng Xiaoping when rival Nationalist forces begin killing communists. Marries first wife Zhang Xianyuan.
1929 - Leads Bose uprising in southwestern Guangxi region, wife Zhang Xianyuan dies in childbirth in Shanghai.
1930 - Leads Longzhou uprising in Guangxi and leads Sevent Red Army to eastern Jiangxi province, losing many men.
1931 - Works closely with Mao Zedong for first time.
1932 - Marries beautiful and energetic Communist Party official Jin Weiying.

1933 - Comes under attack from an anti-Mao faction within the party and is purged, imprisoned and forced to write self-criticisms -- his first fall from political power. Jin Weiying divorces him to marry one of his chief critics.

1934 - Posted in disgrace to Nancun district party committee but then reassigned to the General Political Department of the First Front Army and appointed editor-in-chief of army journal. Takes part in Long March, and develops typhoid. Becomes chief secretary to the party Central Committee.
1937 - Becomes political commissar in 8th Route Army, where he works with Liu Bocheng, one of the communists' top generals.
1939 - Marries Zhuo Lin in Yan'an, a month after meeting her. The couple eventually have two sons and three daughters.
1947 - Together with Liu Bocheng, leads troops across the Yellow River marking the beginning of the communists' counter-offensive against Nationalist forces.
1948 - Deng takes part in Huaihai campaign, where the Eighth Route Army destroys Nationalist army of 550,000 men.
1949 - Together with Liu Bocheng, establishes and organises communist rule in southwest China.
1951 - With Liu, leads "peaceful liberation" by communist troops of Himalayan region of Tibet.
1952 - Promoted to vice premier.
1954 - Gains significant power at the national level with appointment to the post of party secretary-general.
1955 - Elected to the elite Political Bureau of the party Central Committee.
1956 - Becomes a member of Politburo's standing committee and is elected general secretary of the party.
1957 - Travels with Mao Zedong to Moscow. Plays an important role in the Anti-Rightist Campaign, which years later he was to admit was serious mistake.

1961 - First uses the phrase, "It doesn't matter if the cat is black or white, so long as it catches mice" -- which later becomes his catchword -- to justify a return to individual farming after a famine follows collectivisation.
1962 - Criticises Mao-backed people's communes, saying they function poorly; speaks of the damage done to the economy by the Great Leap Forward in speech to high-level conference.
1963 - Returns to Moscow in vain attempt to heal the rift between Moscow and Beijing, appointed acting premier.

1966 - Falls victim to Mao's ultra-leftist Cultural Revolution, is purged from the party leadership by radical Maoists and sent to do manual labour in eastern Jiangxi Province -- his second fall from power.
1969 - Released from labour.
1973 - Returns from political wilderness, is rehabilitated and re-appointed vice-premier.

1974 - Takes over routine work of party and government when Premier Zhou Enlai stricken by cancer. Visits the U.N. General Assembly in New York in visit that is said to open his eyes to the gap between China and the prosperity of Western nations.
1976 - Ousted by Gang of Four led by Mao's wife Jiang Qing -- his third fall from power.
1977 - Reinstated to official posts after the death of Mao and arrest of the Gang of Four.

1978 - Begins policy of reform and opening to the outside world that will transform China from backward Stalinist nation to emerging economic superpower. Sets the terms for the normalisation of relations with the United States.
1979 - Consolidates control over party and state, ousting Mao's designated heir Hua Guofeng. U.S. journal Time magazine names him "Man of the Year".
1981 - Orchestrates passing of resolution by party congress to negate the Cultural Revolution but affirms overall value of Mao's contribution to the Chinese revolution.
1987 - Sacks first appointed heir, party chief Hu Yaobang, blaming him for liberal policy that stirred student demonstrations.
- Retires from the Politburo, Central Committee and Central Advisory Commission.

1989 - Orders army to crush student-led pro-democracy demonstrations centred on Beijing's Tiananmen Square. Many lives lost. Sacks second appointed heir, party chief Zhao Ziyang, for alleged role in the protests and appoints Jiang Zemin.
- Later resigns as head of the Central Military Commission.
1990 - March, he steps down as chairman of the less powerful State Military Commission, his last formal post, but continues to exert great influence from behind the scenes.
1992 - Urges faster development during a tour of south China that takes the post-1989 brakes off China's economy and sparks inflationary boom.
1994 - Makes last public appearence in Shanghai during a tour to mark the Chinese Lunar New Year, appears frail and faltering.
February 19, 1997 - Dies in Beijing of respiratory failure, suffering from advanced stages of Parkinson's disease.
